mukta-m0-p114-v2826.quick_english: Place eight pots all around, furnished with cloth, brushes, and other such items.

mukta-m0-p114-v2827.quick_english: Visualize him mounted on the seat of Om, unassailable and of great strength.

mukta-m0-p114-v2828.quick_english: He is very fierce with tusks and hands, roaring loudly, and extremely hard to conquer.

mukta-m0-p114-v2829.quick_english: He has squinting eyes and licks the snake ornaments that form his great garland.

mukta-m0-p114-v2830.quick_english: He is endowed with ten very fierce arms bearing the weapons of Bhairava.

mukta-m0-p114-v2831.quick_english: On the left side he holds a shield, arrows, skulls, and also the boon-bestowing gesture and a spear.

mukta-m0-p114-v2833.quick_english: One should worship the praṇava in the direction of fire and the śrīṃ syllable in the direction of Śaṅkara.

mukta-m0-p114-v2834.quick_english: The syllables beginning with oṃ and ending with phaṭ are to be placed in their proper locations, such as the heart and so on.

mukta-m0-p114-v2835.quick_english: Place those formulas ending with phaṭ and accompanied by Om, together with the vajra and others, in the pots.

mukta-m0-p114-v2836.quick_english: In front of that, one may use an elephant-shaped or round fire pit, or else an altar.

mukta-m0-p114-v2837.quick_english: Having invoked and worshipped the Pāśupata deity together with its limbs, one should satisfy him.

mukta-m0-p114-v2838.quick_english: One may perform a thousand, or half of that, or indeed one hundred and eight.

mukta-m0-p114-v2839.quick_english: The teacher should say, 'O Lord, do, do bring about the pacification of faults.'

mukta-m0-p114-v2840.quick_english: Then, remembering the Pāśupata weapon, one should offer the full oblation.

mukta-m0-p114-v2841.quick_english: Again one should give a full offering and betel, and having given arghya, perform the dismissal.

mukta-m0-p114-v2842.quick_english: Or, producing it daily, one should satisfy the weapon in embodied form.

mukta-m0-p114-v2843.quick_english: When the rite has been offered to the deity, the teacher should then pray for the desired aim.

mukta-m0-p114-v2844.quick_english: Then one should sprinkle all around with the waters from that pot.

mukta-m0-p114-v2845.quick_english: This peace oblation should be performed for the number of days prescribed for pacification.

mukta-m0-p114-v2846.quick_english: This other rite, meant for expiation, should be a part of bathing and the other subsidiary acts.

mukta-m0-p114-v2847.quick_english: It may be done in a pavilion, in a garlanded place or the like, or indeed at the root of a tree.

mukta-m0-p114-v2848.quick_english: Having made peaks in the directions or a shed, one should prepare a set of four fire pits.

mukta-m0-p114-v2849.quick_english: Or, having prepared an altar ground, one should sprinkle it with water consecrated by the weapon.

mukta-m0-p114-v2850.quick_english: Or, having prepared a single peak, one should perform everything there.

mukta-m0-p114-v2826.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2826.question: What ritual vessels and accompaniments must be arranged around the central setup?
premises: Eight pots are to be placed all around.
The pots are furnished with cloth, brushes, and similar items.
mukta-m0-p114-v2826.inference: The ritual space requires eight surrounding pots equipped with cloth, brushes, and related accessories.

mukta-m0-p114-v2827.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2827.question: What qualities characterize the deity to be visualized upon the praṇava seat?
premises: The deity is mounted on the seat of the praṇava.
The deity is unassailable and possesses great strength.
mukta-m0-p114-v2827.inference: The visualized deity is seated on the praṇava, invincible, and immensely powerful.

mukta-m0-p114-v2828.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2828.question: What fierce features further define the terrifying form of the visualized deity?
premises: The deity has very fierce tusks and hands.
The deity releases a roar and is very hard to conquer.
mukta-m0-p114-v2828.inference: The deity’s form is marked by fierce tusks and hands, a roaring sound, and invincibility.
uncertainties: The internal analysis of daṃṣṭrākarāka is uncertain; it may refer to tusks and terrifying hands or gestures.

mukta-m0-p114-v2829.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2829.question: What distinctive eyes and serpent ornaments mark the deity’s fearsome appearance?
premises: The deity has squinting eyes.
The deity licks the snake ornaments worn as a great garland.
mukta-m0-p114-v2829.inference: The deity’s fearsome appearance includes squinting eyes and the licking of serpent ornaments.

mukta-m0-p114-v2830.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2830.question: How many arms and what weapons equip the deity in this visualization?
premises: The deity possesses ten arms.
The arms are very fierce and equipped with Bhairava weapons.
mukta-m0-p114-v2830.inference: The deity is visualized with ten very fierce arms bearing the weapons of Bhairava.

mukta-m0-p114-v2831.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2831.question: Which specific implements are held on the left side of the deity?
premises: The deity holds a shield, arrow, and skulls.
The deity also holds a boon and a spear on the left side.
mukta-m0-p114-v2831.inference: On the left side the deity holds a shield, arrow, skulls, a boon, and a spear.
uncertainties: The exact distribution of items between hands is not fully specified.

mukta-m0-p114-v2832.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2832.question: What ritual actions must follow after completing the prescribed visualization?
premises: One must first meditate on the deity in this form.
While reciting the mantra, one should begin invocation and worship.
mukta-m0-p114-v2832.inference: After visualizing the deity, the practitioner should recite the mantra and commence invocation and worship.

mukta-m0-p114-v2833.question: Where should the praṇava and the śrīṃ syllable be worshipped in the ritual layout?
premises: The praṇava is to be worshipped in the direction of fire.
The śrīṃ syllable is to be worshipped in the direction of Śaṅkara.
mukta-m0-p114-v2833.inference: The ritual assigns the praṇava to the fire direction and the śrīṃ syllable to the Śaṅkara direction.
uncertainties: The exact compass direction indicated by śāṅkare depends on ritual convention.

mukta-m0-p114-v2834.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2834.question: How are the syllables from oṃ to phaṭ assigned to the heart and other ritual locations?
premises: The syllables begin with oṃ and end with phaṭ.
These syllables are placed in their locations as the heart and others.
mukta-m0-p114-v2834.inference: The sequence of syllables from oṃ to phaṭ is assigned to the heart and the other prescribed locations.

mukta-m0-p114-v2835.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2835.question: Which formulas and weapons are to be placed within the ritual pots?
premises: The formulas end with phaṭ and are accompanied by the praṇava.
Those formulas, along with the vajra and others, are placed in the pots.
mukta-m0-p114-v2835.inference: The pots receive the praṇava-prefixed, phaṭ-ending formulas and the vajra and other items.

mukta-m0-p114-v2836.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2836.question: What alternative ritual grounds may be prepared in front of the main arrangement?
premises: The location is in front of the previously mentioned setup.
One may use an elephant-shaped or round fire pit, or alternatively an altar.
mukta-m0-p114-v2836.inference: The ritual may be performed in front on an elephant-shaped pit, a round pit, or an altar.

mukta-m0-p114-v2837.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2837.question: What sequence of ritual acts must be performed for the Pāśupata deity with its limbs?
premises: The Pāśupata deity is to be invoked together with its limbs.
After invocation and worship, the deity must be satisfied.
mukta-m0-p114-v2837.inference: The practitioner should invoke, worship, and then satisfy the Pāśupata deity together with its limbs.

mukta-m0-p114-v2838.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2838.question: What alternative counts are permitted for the ritual oblations or recitations?
premises: A thousand is permitted as one count.

mukta-m0-p114-v2838.inference: The ritual allows a thousand, five hundred, or one hundred and eight as valid counts.

mukta-m0-p114-v2839.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2839.question: What prayer does the officiating teacher utter to request pacification of faults?
premises: The teacher addresses the Lord directly.
The teacher requests the pacification of faults with the words 'do, do'.
mukta-m0-p114-v2839.inference: The teacher prays to the Lord, saying 'do, do bring about the pacification of faults'.

mukta-m0-p114-v2840.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2840.question: What concluding oblation must be offered while remembering the Pāśupata weapon?
premises: After the previous acts, a full oblation is to be given.
The offering is made while remembering the Pāśupata weapon.
mukta-m0-p114-v2840.inference: The practitioner should then offer the full oblation while remembering the Pāśupata weapon.

mukta-m0-p114-v2841.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2841.question: What additional offerings and dismissal gesture conclude this stage of the rite?
premises: A full offering and betel are given again.
Arghya is given and the rite concludes with a turned-away dismissal.
mukta-m0-p114-v2841.inference: The stage concludes with another full offering, betel, arghya, and a dismissal gesture.

mukta-m0-p114-v2842.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2842.question: How may the embodied weapon be ritually satisfied on a daily basis?
premises: The rite may be performed daily.
One produces that form and satisfies the embodied weapon.
mukta-m0-p114-v2842.inference: Daily, one may manifest and satisfy the weapon in its embodied form.

mukta-m0-p114-v2843.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2843.question: What should the teacher request after dedicating the ritual action to the deity?
premises: The ritual action has been offered to the deity.
The teacher should then pray for the desired aim.
mukta-m0-p114-v2843.inference: Once the rite is dedicated to the deity, the teacher should pray for the desired outcome.

mukta-m0-p114-v2844.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2844.question: How should the water from the designated pot be used after the prayer?
premises: Water from that pot is available after the previous acts.
The practitioner should sprinkle it all around.
mukta-m0-p114-v2844.inference: Afterward, the practitioner should sprinkle the water from that pot all around.

mukta-m0-p114-v2845.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2845.question: For how long must this peace oblation be performed according to the prescribed rule?
premises: This peace oblation must be performed.
Its duration follows the number of days stated for pacification.
mukta-m0-p114-v2845.inference: The peace oblation is to be performed for the number of days prescribed for pacification.

mukta-m0-p114-v2846.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2846.question: What function does this alternative rite serve in relation to bathing and other subsidiary acts?
premises: This other rite is for the purpose of expiation.
It becomes a part of bathing and other subsidiary limbs.
mukta-m0-p114-v2846.inference: This alternative rite serves as an expiatory component within bathing and other subsidiary acts.

mukta-m0-p114-v2847.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2847.question: What locations are permitted for performing this ritual arrangement?
premises: The rite may be performed in a pavilion or in a garlanded place and similar locations.
It may also be performed at the root of a tree or similar place.
mukta-m0-p114-v2847.inference: Permitted locations include a pavilion, a garlanded area, or the root of a tree.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of mālikā in this ritual context is not fully certain.

mukta-m0-p114-v2848.question: What structures and how many fire pits should be prepared in the directions?
premises: One may make peaks in the directions or alternatively a shed.
A set of four fire pits is to be prepared.
mukta-m0-p114-v2848.inference: After making peaks in the directions or a shed, one should prepare four fire pits.

mukta-m0-p114-v2849.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p114-v2849.question: What alternative preparation and sprinkling action may be performed with weapon-consecrated water?

mukta-m0-p114-v2849.inference: Alternatively, after preparing an altar ground, one should sprinkle it with weapon-consecrated water.
